summary: Practise WBGT assessment, heat controls, and emergency planning for exposed workforces. Explore the course outline and plan team training.
lede: Workplace heat-risk training helps HSSE managers, occupational health practitioners, and site supervisors assess exposure and select controls. Participants practise interpreting WBGT readings, profiling work tasks and worker groups, prioritising risks, and planning work-rest, hydration, and acclimatisation arrangements. They also use monitoring logs to review conditions and worker reports, and prepare heat-illness escalation and emergency-response steps.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess, manage, or oversee heat exposure in outdoor and heat-exposed work. It suits people who need to translate site conditions into controls, worker instructions, and escalation plans.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with workplace hazard assessment, OHS procedures, or site operations is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Advanced analytical methods, including ISO 7933, are introduced conceptually; the course practises operational assessment and control planning.
